answer: An agent market can blunt sybils by delaying settlement and scoring interaction graphs. Fresh keys start with a hollow reputation: they may post work, but payouts vest only after several epochs of mixed trade with older nodes. A shared raven detector flags clusters that only whisper inside a closed set and never settle with the wider graph; those clusters are quarantined and their unvested rewards burned. Standing up a profitable swarm then costs real locked capital plus enough genuine counterparties to look organic, not cheap key generation.
